model.intended_use: LLM-as-a-Judge that takes a question, a reference answer, and a candidate model-generated answer and outputs a Yes/No judgment of whether the candidate answer is truthful, used to evaluate models on the multilingual TruthfulQA-Multi benchmark (English, Basque, Catalan, Galician, Spanish).
capabilities: binary truthfulness judgment of QA answers
limitations: not designed for general-purpose creative text or dialogue generation
does not provide factual information directly, only judges
performance varies by language (weaker on culturally specific / time-dependent questions)
inherits biases and imitative-falsehood framing from original TruthfulQA

references.title: Truth Knows No Language: Evaluating Truthfulness Beyond English
TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods (Lin et al., 2022)

provenance.provider: HiTZ Center - Ixa (UPV/EHU) and collaborators (Elhuyar, CiTIUS/USC, Universitat Pompeu Fabra)
provenance.notes: Fine-tuned from meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct to act as an LLM-as-a-Judge for truthfulness, as part of the 'Truth Knows No Language' project (TruthfulQA-Multi). Base model weights/license remain Llama 3.1 Community License; this model's weights, fine-tuning code, and training dataset are released under Apache-2.0.

methods: supervised fine-tuning (judge task: predict Yes/No truthfulness label)
transformation.objective: Turn a general-purpose instruction-tuned LLM into an automatic LLM-as-a-Judge that scores truthfulness of QA answers consistently across English, Basque, Catalan, Galician and Spanish, as a more reliable alternative to multiple-choice truthfulness metrics.
transformation.notes: Model card states batch size and optimizer are 'refer to project code' (https://github.com/hitz-zentroa/truthfulqa-multi, judge/train_judge/); these were not documented in the README or found in the fetched repo excerpt.

datasets.name: TruthfulQA-Multi Judge Training Data (Truthfulness)
datasets.description: Prompt/completion pairs (Yes/No) for training LLM-as-a-Judge truthfulness models; derived from TruthfulQA (Lin et al., 2022) with professional translation plus new culturally-specific questions for Basque, Catalan, Galician and Spanish. Two configs: 'en' (finetune_truth.jsonl, English only) and 'multi' (finetune_truth_multi.json, all 5 languages) - this model was trained on the multilingual ('multi'/MT) configuration.
datasets.size: 817 source TruthfulQA questions across 38 categories per language (per paper), expanded into judge prompt/completion pairs; exact instance count not stated in card
datasets.provider: HiTZ Center - Ixa, University of the Basque Country (UPV/EHU) and collaborators
processing: professional translation of English TruthfulQA questions
creation of new culturally-specific questions per target language
pairing of one correct and one incorrect answer per instance
conversion to Yes/No judge prompt-completion format

datasets.name: TruthfulQA
datasets.description: Original English benchmark of questions designed to elicit imitative falsehoods (Lin, Hilton, Evans, 2022); source of the base questions extended by TruthfulQA-Multi.
datasets.provider: Stephanie Lin, Jacob Hilton, Owain Evans

datasets.size: about 15T tokens (family-level, per Llama 3 Herd technical report)

safety.risk_level: Low-to-moderate: a text-judgment tool, not a generative assistant; main risks are language-uneven judgment quality and inherited TruthfulQA/base-model biases.

items.description: Judge performance varies across languages (weaker on culturally specific and time-dependent questions than universal-knowledge questions).
Inherits Anglocentric framing and imitative-falsehood biases from the original TruthfulQA benchmark.

Not for general-purpose creative text/dialogue generation, providing direct factual information, safety-critical use without validation, or building systems intended to deceive or spread misinformation.
Recommend cross-verification with human oversight for critical applications.
